description: Until now you have gone down to Rustmoor through the hole in No. 9's floor, the way the rats go. Today you go by the gate, the way people go, in Hester's oilskin from the peg behind the door. A tip-keeper in three coats turns his book round for you to sign. Everyone signs in going out onto the heaps, and signs out coming back. This page was begun eight weeks ago. Most names have both. Four have only the first, each ruled off, and those four never came back. Their things wait on the shelf behind him, tied in string. "Name," he says. "Business. And next of kin, for if you're the fifth."

options.label: Give Professor Brassbuckle as your next of kin.

success.text: The tip-keeper writes it down without comment, and leaves a space under it for the ruler, which is somehow worse than comment. Word of it reaches the Polytechnic ahead of you. Brassbuckle does not mention it, but a parcel from the Polytechnic comes with a note in her hand, "Come back in one piece," underlined twice, and an extra Ration.
success.note: Everyone going onto the Rustmoor heaps signs the tip book at the gate, and signs out coming back. A name never signed out is someone who did not come back.

options.label: Write "No. 9 Sprocket Row" for your next of kin.

success.text: "A workshop," says the tip-keeper. "Can't say I've had that one." He writes it in anyway, in capitals. "If you're the fifth," he says, "we'll send your spanner home." He means it kindly, and to show it he gives you a Ration from inside the second coat.
